title.narrative: Promoting local development and reducing regional asymmetries in Cabo Verde

description.narrative: Cabo Verde has experienced a positive path towards sustainable development for more than two decades. It has been ranking within the top 11 African countries in human development and classified within medium income countries since 2008. However, the country remains vulnerable vi-a-vis to external shocks owing to its high dependency on tourism and imported intermediary and final goods. In the past couple of years, multiple crises came to challenge these development progresses: COVID-19, with a socio-economic impact amongst the highest in the world, led to a decrease of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) by 14.8%, public revenues by 25%, and an increase in unemployment by 3.2% ; climate change impacts on biodiversity and food security as changing weather patterns (especially droughts) influence agricultural production and ocean warming with decreasing fish stocks; and the war in Ukraine, with devastating effects on the economy that is heavily relying on fossil fuels to operate, and negative consequences for the purchasing power of the households, especially the most vulnerable, as 80% of the food is imported. Vulnerable groups are the most affected: 32% of the population are still living under the poverty line with 13% being extreme poor. But not all islands and communities are equally affected. There is significant territorial inequality. Cabo Verde adopted a decentralization reform with the aim to promote national cohesion by reducing regional asymmetries, improving effectiveness of public policies, and allowing citizens to better have their rights fulfilled. In the new National Strategic Development Plan (PEDS II 2022-2026), the main outcome expected in this area is: “by 2026, 100% of municipalities have adopted results-based planning and budgeting instruments”. The new United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) 2023-2027 is aligned to that vision, with one of the three strategic areas, “Transformative governance and strengthened territorial cohesion”, tackling the problem of territorial inequality. Significant progress has been achieved concerning decentralisation during the last five years. Each municipality has defined its agenda for local sustainable development via the Municipal Strategic Sustainable Development Plans (PEMDS), established participation mechanisms (the Local Platforms) and built the capacity of local actors. This present Joint Programme (JP) builds upon this work to accelerate local development by tackling some of the main issues that remain in place, including in particular the limited capacity of local authorities to generate own-source revenues, to manage effectively and efficiently existing resources (including natural resources) and to effectively engage local populations in local development agenda as well as to allow them to better access basic services and economic infrastructures and assets. Based on the theory of change, identifying the assumptions as outputs, the purpose of this JP is to reduce regional asymmetries and promote local development in Cabo Verde, in line with the new territorial cohesion policy. Three outcomes are expected: (i) Local authorities have increased own-source revenues; (ii) Action by local authorities has improved positive social, economic and environmental impact; (iii) Local development projects are more responsive to local needs and potentials. One of the takeaways from the precedent experiences concerning decentralisation in Cabo Verde is the importance on putting local actors at the centre of action as a way to build reforms ensuring their ownership and as condition to their successful long-term application. Therefore, this JP deepens the engagement of local actors as well as associations of municipalities in the decentralisation process, to allow for institutionalisation of positive impacts. The Joint Programme implementation will be overseen by a Steering Committee and led by a Joint Programme Management Team. On the United Nations side, the Resident Coordinator’s Office (RCO) will lead the steering process while United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) will collaboratively implement the project activities. Important to note that UN-Habitat will lead Outcome 1, whilst the other two will be executed by UNDP. In addition, UN-Habitat will have an involvement in the Outcome 3, particularly in the execution of the activity 3.1.3. (Develop Productive Development Plans for the 9 islands), based on previous work supporting the elaboration of the Islands’ Economic Specialization Profile carried out by Ministry of Territorial Cohesion.
